t: This is the site of Faraday House, a former electrical engineering college, named after the scientist Michael Faraday. It trained engineers in power generation and distribution, at a time before engineering was widely taught at universities. It began as an adjunct to a company supplying towns with electricity, and it operated from 1889 to 1967, mainly on Southampton Row. Six of its alumni went on to become presidents of the Institution of Electrical Engineers. Faraday himself was a self-taught pioneer of electromagnetism and electrolysis, which is why his name suited a college built for the electrical age.
